blockerRepairAudit.finding: CLAUDE-G18-V1-B1 — EV-5's exactByteIntent enumerated five GC roots and omitted active/provisional generations entirely (the word 'provisional' occurred nowhere in v1), while binding retention policy/tombstones was named only in measures and never carried into the retained root set. EV-5's measures also made an express but short-by-one enumeration of what file 04's reachability list adds beyond the generation-property bullet.
blockerRepairAudit.method: File 04 lines 123-139 were re-read live this cycle and the five bullets extracted, then compared to the subject's enumeration and to its retained root list. Not read against v1's account or against my own earlier verdict.
blockerRepairAudit.measuresRepair: measures now reads 'File 04 reachability (lines 123-139) names five roots: project/operation locks and active generation leases; retained authoritative evidence and custody records; active/provisional generations and rollback slots; prepared migrations and repair state; and binding retention policy/tombstones.' That is all five live bullets, in the live order, with both halves of each intact and each slash-joined phrase kept whole. The short-by-one delta sentence is gone, replaced by the full enumeration — which is the stronger repair, since it no longer depends on the reader trusting a delta claim at all. It also improves the attribution of the first quotation, which now reads '(file 04 generation-property bullet)' rather than a bare '(file 04)', so the two file-04 statements of the removal obligation are distinguished by name.
blockerRepairAudit.exactByteIntentRepair: The retained root set is now 'project/operation locks, active generation leases, preview-honest retained-evidence/custody records, active/provisional generations, rollback slots, prepared migrations, binding retention policy/tombstones', with 'The repair-state root remains joined to DR-110/G08' in the following sentence. Mapping that against the five live bullets: bullet 1 both halves present; bullet 2 present as the preview-scoped rendering; bullet 3 BOTH halves now present, including the previously absent active/provisional generations; bullet 4 both halves present, prepared migrations in the list and repair state named as a root and routed; bullet 5 present. All ten halves of the five bullets are accounted for. The failure scenario I set out at v1 — a provisional generation between migration prepare and commit, held by no lock, no lease, not retained evidence, not a rollback slot and not itself a prepared migration, reachable from nothing under the old root set — no longer exists: it is now a named root in its own right.
blockerRepairAudit.twoRoutedHalves: Two halves are named but not retained here, each with a stated reason I checked against the source. The authoritative-evidence half is scoped to 'whatever operational-metadata / doctor records DR-124 assigns', because D-002 defers DR-106/109/113 wholly so the preview ships no authoritative sealed closure. The repair-state half is routed to DR-110/G08, because D-002 defers DR-110 self-update/repair. Both routings are parallel in shape, both are sourced to D-002's deferrals, and both were present in v1 in the same form — I accepted them then and the reasoning is unchanged. Routing a root the preview cannot have, with the reason stated, is not the same defect as dropping a root the preview does have.
